div.head: Af El. 17
div.ab: Se þe his agenne slea þeowne esne oððe his wifman, ⁊ he ne sy idæges dead, þeah he libbe twa nyht oððe þreo, ne byþ he ealles swa scyldig, forðam hit wæs his agen þeow. Gif he þonne byð idæges dead, þonne sitte seo scyld on him.

Se ðe slea his agenne þeowne esne oððe his mennen, ⁊ he ne sie idæges dead, ðeah he libbe twa niht oððe ðreo, ne bið he ealles swa scyldig, forþon þe hit wæs his agen fioh. Gif he ðonne sie idæges dead, ðonne sitte sio scyld on him.
Qui percusserit seruum uel ancillam suam uirga, et mortui fuerint in manibus eius, criminis reus erit. Sin autem uno die superuixerit uel duobus, non subiacebit penæ, quia pecunia illius est.

Se ðe slea his agenne þeowne esne oððe his mennen, ⁊ he ne sie idæges dead, ðeah he libbe twa niht oððe ðreo, ne bið he ealles swa scyldig, forþon þe hit wæs his agen fioh. Gif he ðonne sie idæges dead, ðonne sitte sio scyld on him.

He who strikes his own slave or maidservant, and he [or she] is not dead on that same day, though [the servant] should live for two days or three, the master will not be entirely so guilty, because it was his own loss. If the servant, however, should die on the same day, then let the guilt rest on him [i.e., the master].

Wer seinen eigenen Sklavenknecht oder seine Sklavin schlägt, und die Person ist nicht selbigen Tages todt, wenn sie noch zwei Nächte oder drei lebt, so ist jener nicht ganz so schuldig, weil es seine eigene Fahrhabe war. Wenn die Person aber selbigen Tages todt ist, dann liege die Schuld auf ihm.

Whoever strikes his own slave-servant or his slave woman, and the person is not dead the same day, if he still lives two nights or three, then he is not quite so guilty, because it was his own property. But if the person is dead the same day, then let the guilt lie upon him.
